name: Cable glute kickback
cue: Brace, then kick straight back; do not arch.
research: Standing cable glute kickback (hip extension), right leg working, facing the column. Design values from the standard technique description, not a measured trial. The left leg stands (knee 4, the sole flat on the plate), both hands are on a horizontal grab bar of the column (0.3 H ahead of the stance, 0.6 H high, the elbows bent about 63 deg), the trunk 20 deg forward as one line from the hips (pelvis 14, lumbar 3, thorax 3) and the pelvis level. An ankle cuff (0.04 H in radius, 0.07 to 0.11 H above the ankle) on the right ankle carries a ring on its front; the cable runs from the low pulley (0.075 H, 0.48 H ahead of the stance and 0.07 H to the right, on a fork on the column's base) to the ring, so it pulls the ankle forward and the leg is driven back against it. The working knee stays slightly bent (28 to 32 deg, which keeps the foot clear of the plate) while the hip goes from 42 deg of flexion (thigh about 22 deg ahead of the vertical, the foot 0.11 H ahead of the hip) to 2 deg, the thigh about 18 deg behind the vertical and the foot 0.22 H behind the hip, with the trunk and the pelvis still so the lower back does not arch. The cable is nearly horizontal throughout, so the leg is loaded the whole sweep: the moment arm against the cable, the sine of the angle between the leg and the cable, is 0.98 at the start, 0.96 mid-range and 0.79 at the end. Cable 1:1 to the stack. Geometry: design/cableB/sk.mjs glute.

targets.note: design values (standard technique), not a measured trial: the trunk stays still, the hip extends

camera.note: From behind and to the right (az 120, el 8, 30 deg from the right profile): the right gluteus maximus faces the camera and the leg swinging back stays in profile, so the whole kick reads; the column, the grab bar and the cable stand in front of the figure and stay in frame.

skinChecks.note: the standing foot stays flat on the plate
